title: Reported Speech — Statements & Basic Backshift
subtitle: Report what someone said, without quoting their exact words.
objectives: Use say and tell correctly (tell always needs a listener)
Backshift the verb tense one step into the past when reporting
Change time and place words (today, here, tomorrow) to fit the new point of view
Report simple statements without needing every reporting-verb pattern yet

content.intro: When you tell someone what another person said, you usually don't repeat their exact words — you report the idea, from your own point of view, later in time. This changes the verb tense and a few other words.

rules.heading: a) Say vs. tell
rules.body:
say (no listener needed, or use "to" + listener) and tell (always needs a listener, no "to")

  • She said, "I'm tired." → She said (that) she was tired.
  • She said to me, "I'm tired." → She told me (that) she was tired.
  • Never say “She said me” — use “told me” or “said to me.”

rules.heading: b) Backshifting the verb
rules.body:
When the reporting verb (said, told) is in the past, the reported verb usually moves one step further into the past too:

  • Present simple → past simple: "I work here." → He said he worked there.
  • Present continuous → past continuous: "I'm working." → He said he was working.
  • Past simple → past perfect: "I finished." → He said he had finished.
  • Present perfect → past perfect: "I have finished." → He said he had finished.
  • can → could, will → would: "I can help." → He said he could help.

rules.heading: c) Changing time, place and pronouns
rules.body:
Words that point to "now" or "here" from the original speaker's moment usually change too, since you're reporting later, from a different point of view:

  • today → that day  |  tomorrow → the next day / the following day  |  yesterday → the day before
  • here → there  |  now → then
  • this → that  |  my/I → his/her/etc. (the pronoun changes to match who is being reported)

examples: "I'm hungry," she said. → She said (that) she was hungry.
"We live in Porto Alegre," they said. → They said (that) they lived in Porto Alegre.
"I saw him yesterday," he told me. → He told me (that) he had seen him the day before.
"I'll call you tomorrow," she said. → She said (that) she would call me the next day.
"I can't come today," he said. → He said (that) he couldn't come that day.
"I have already finished," she told us. → She told us (that) she had already finished.
"I'm studying here," he said. → He said (that) he was studying there.
"This is my book," she said. → She said (that) that was her book.

commonMistakes.wrong: She said me she was tired.
commonMistakes.right: She told me she was tired. / She said (to me) she was tired.
commonMistakes.why: "Say" never takes a direct listener without "to" — use "tell" for that, or add "to" before the listener.
With a past reporting verb (said), the present tense usually backshifts to the past.

commonMistakes.wrong: She said she will call tomorrow.
commonMistakes.right: She said she would call the next day.
commonMistakes.why: "Will" backshifts to "would," and "tomorrow" (from her original moment) becomes "the next day" from your later point of view.

commonMistakes.wrong: He told that he was busy.
commonMistakes.right: He told me (that) he was busy. / He said (that) he was busy.
commonMistakes.why: "Tell" needs a listener (told me, told her); without one, use "said."
"Here" (her location, at the time) becomes "there" from your point of view, and "is" backshifts to "was."

exercises.title: Fill in the Blanks
exercises.instructions: Complete each reported sentence with the correct backshifted verb.

items.prompt: "I am busy," he said. → He said he ___ busy.
items.explanation: Present simple (am) backshifts to past simple (was).

items.prompt: "We are watching a film," they said. → They said they ___ watching a film.
items.explanation: Present continuous backshifts to past continuous.

items.prompt: "I finished my homework," she said. → She said she ___ finished her homework.
items.explanation: Past simple backshifts to past perfect (had + past participle).

items.prompt: "I can swim," he said. → He said he ___ swim.
"I will help you," she told me. → She told me she ___ help me.
"I have never been to Rio," he said. → He said he ___ never been to Rio.
items.explanation: Present perfect backshifts to past perfect.

items.incorrect: She said me she was cold.
answer: She told me she was cold.
She said to me she was cold.
items.explanation: "Say" needs "to" before a listener, or use "tell" instead, which never takes "to."

answer: He told me he was leaving.
items.explanation: "Tell" always needs a listener object (told me/us/her); without one, use "said."

items.incorrect: They said they will arrive today.
answer: They said they would arrive that day.
items.explanation: "Will" backshifts to "would," and "today" (from their original moment) becomes "that day."
The present tense backshifts to the past after a past reporting verb.

exercises.title: Report the Sentence
exercises.instructions: Rewrite each quoted sentence as reported speech.

answer: She said she was working late that night.

items.prompt: "We saw the movie yesterday," they told me.
answer: They told me they had seen the movie the day before.
items.explanation: Past simple → past perfect; "yesterday" → "the day before."

items.prompt: "I can't come to the party," he said.
answer: He said he couldn't come to the party.
She said she would finish it the next day.

summary: Say has no listener (or “to” + listener); tell always needs a listener, with no “to.”
After a past reporting verb, tenses backshift one step into the past (am → was, finished → had finished, will → would).
Time/place words shift point of view: today → that day, tomorrow → the next day, here → there.
This is the foundation for more complex reported speech (questions, commands, and reporting-verb patterns like deny/urge/warn) taught later.
